name: Croatian nationalism
summary: Croatian nationalism holds that the Croats are a nation with a continuous, historic right to their own sovereign state, from medieval statehood through the Party of Rights to Tuđman's independence in 1991. In its mainstream form it is conservative, Catholic-leaning and anti-communist, and it has become pro-EU and pro-NATO. Its radical wing, the Ustase, added ethnic exclusion and genocide and is a disowned extreme rather than the mainstream.
scope: The mainstream tradition: Starčević's Party of Rights state-right doctrine, Radić's peasant movement, and Tuđman's HDZ and its present Christian-democratic form, as set out in the 1990 constitution. It excludes the Ustase regime of 1941-45 and Greater Croatia irredentism except where noted. Economic and social answers are largely inferred from HDZ practice.

sources.usedFor: Founder of the right-wing tradition: state right, broad Croat identity, anti-feudalism, secularism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: HDZ governments have raised the minimum wage modestly while courting business; the nationalist core has no wage doctrine and adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The constitution makes entrepreneurial and market freedom the basis of the economy, yet HDZ privatisation was state-steered and favoured insiders; adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalists in the Tuđman era were wary of unions as relics of socialist self-management, while later HDZ governments negotiated with them; no settled line.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution guarantees ownership, but allows limits for the general welfare and expropriation with market compensation, so strong but not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nationalists focus on who owns firms rather than regulation in general; HDZ governments have mixed regulation and business-friendliness.

cut-welfare.rationale: HDZ rule has kept pensions and veterans' benefits generous, and Catholic-conservative adherents favour family support, so cuts are not a core aim.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Croatia has hate-speech laws, but nationalists commonly resist their use against symbols and slogans of the Homeland War and the Ustaše-era controversy; split.

strong-leader.rationale: Tuđmanism built a dominant presidency with tight control over the state and media, and Tuđman cast himself as the father of the nation who made independence possible.

state-harmful.rationale: Croatian nationalism centres on winning and defending a state of its own, grounded in a historic state right; the state is the instrument of national existence.

empower-police-military.rationale: Tuđman-era policy built up the armed forces and security services around the independence war, and nationalists treat the Homeland War army as a founding institution.

decide-locally.rationale: The constitution declares Croatia a unitary state and Tuđman centralised power; the movement's history is about a single national state, not devolution.

traditional-family.rationale: HDZ is a Christian-democratic, conservative party that campaigned for the 2013 referendum defining marriage as a man-woman union, treating the family as the base of the nation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: HDZ and nationalist parties backed the 2013 constitutional definition of marriage as between a man and a woman and oppose same-sex marriage, accepting only partnership rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Croatia's law is liberal and HDZ has not repealed it, but Catholic-conservative and nationalist adherents commonly oppose abortion; contested.

more-religion-public.rationale: HDZ's 'God and Croats' slogan and ties to the Catholic Church tie national identity to Catholicism, though the constitution formally separates church and state.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Identity grounded in a continuous Croatian nation, language and Central European civilisation is the core of the ideology, and the Croatian Spring was fought over language.

gradual-change.rationale: Nationalists were radical in the independence break yet conservative in governing; the sources give no clear line.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Tuđman clashed with the international community over Bosnia, while later HDZ is pro-EU and pro-NATO but wary of supranational reach; mildly opposed to more UN power.

nation-first.rationale: Tuđman put the Croatian national interest, including partition of Bosnia, ahead of international pressure; later HDZ cooperates but still frames policy around the nation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Croats sought Western intervention against Serb forces in 1991-95, but Tuđman's own policies were criticised abroad; adherents have no general line.

open-borders.rationale: A national state of the Croatian nation, with border control as an expression of sovereignty, is incompatible with open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: HDZ governments follow EU climate policy without making it a priority, and the nationalist tradition does not address it.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Croatia co-owns the Krško plant in Slovenia, but no nationalist position on expansion is documented; adherents are split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nationalists see the 1990-91 break from Yugoslavia as legitimate, yet condemn communist revolution; the 'revolution' label divides adherents.

central-planning.rationale: Nationalists defined themselves against the communist order, and Tuđman-era HDZ privatised the Yugoslav economy.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalists favour protecting domestic enterprise in principle, but Croatia accepted EU free-trade rules; split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Tuđman-era HDZ steered privatisation toward party-linked owners, so state direction existed in practice, but there is no doctrine of it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Starčević-era and Radić-era traditions prized peasant smallholders, but the modern movement has no stated distributist line.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money and wages is a communist aim that nationalism rejects outright.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Croatia's central bank is firmly part of the state order and euro membership; no nationalist case against it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Tuđman's HDZ dominated the 1990s with authoritarian traits, but formal multiparty democracy was a founding claim and one-party rule is not the creed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The modern movement is republican, and the constitution establishes a republic, though the historical state right tradition includes the medieval kingdom.

democracy-best.rationale: The constitution makes Croatia a democratic state and HDZ has embraced democratic procedure, though Tuđman's rule was criticised as illiberal.

direct-votes.rationale: The constitution uses referendums for major questions such as association and EU entry, and HDZ allies backed the 2013 referendum, but there is no general doctrine.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is the Yugoslav-communist model nationalism rejected.

right-to-secede.rationale: The preamble affirms the Croatian nation's right to secession and association, and the 1991 independence rests on it; adherents apply it chiefly to Croatia itself.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nationalists treat the Homeland War as a just defensive war, and radical strands honour violent figures; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Homeland War memory is sacred to adherents, but the sources do not record a doctrine that war builds character.

separate-church-state.rationale: The constitution says religious communities are separated from the state, yet nationalists tie Croatian identity to Catholicism and the Church; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitution makes law secular; Christian-democratic HDZ draws on Catholic values but does not claim law should be based on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A national state built on sovereign statehood and a national army cannot accept privatised courts and defence.

military-superiority.rationale: The Homeland War shaped a strong-army ethos, but Croatia is a small NATO member; no stated superiority aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The constitution defines Croatia as the national state of the Croatian nation, with minorities' equality; the exclusive version is the Ustase one, outside the mainstream.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism sees the nation, not class, as the unit of history, and rejected the communist order.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not an issue the sources address; conservative parties stress opportunity and merit.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not a Croatian question; the closest analogue, autochthonous minorities, is a different matter, so this is neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Tuđman placed Croatia in Central European and Mediterranean civilisation and later joined the EU and NATO, yet the constitution bars a new Balkan union; split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Conservative and Christian-democratic communitarianism leans toward duty to the nation, but it is an inference rather than a documented position.

limit-population.rationale: Croatia faces emigration and low births, and nationalists worry about demographic decline; they favour more births.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not part of the tradition; nationalists favour development.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement seeks national revival and historical continuity, but modern adherents mostly do not claim restoring a lost social order outranks progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: HDZ has been pragmatic in government, yet nationalists remain ideologically driven; split.

direct-action.rationale: The movement achieved its aims by elections and then war, and the party works through parliament.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No tradition could endorse it; a nation-building movement is wedded to the modern state.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist formula contrary to the market and property framework the constitution adopts.

production-for-use.rationale: Constitution bases the economy on entrepreneurial and market freedom.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim nationalism rejects; Tuđman-era HDZ built a capitalist economy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Croatian nationalism arose against communist Yugoslavia, and Tito purged the Croatian Spring reformers.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation was a communist policy, and the peasant tradition from Radić prized individual smallholding.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Leninist thesis that nationalists reject; they see wars as arising from rival nationalisms, as with Milošević's Serbia.

taxation-theft.rationale: The constitution guarantees ownership but accepts taxation and a social state; libertarian absolutism is not part of the movement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The constitution grants rights to individuals but also gives minorities and the Croatian nation collective standing and cultural autonomy, and nationalism rests on collective rights.

conscription.rationale: Croatia fought the Homeland War with mass mobilisation and abolished conscription only in 2008; adherents see defence as a national duty.

state-as-business.rationale: Nothing in the sources shows the movement framing government as a business; HDZ practice mixed party patronage with state enterprises, so adherents have no clear line.

positive-liberty.rationale: The constitution defines Croatia as a social state, but the nationalist tradition has no positive-liberty doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Starčević's racial language is debated, and the Ustase held Aryan theory, but mainstream modern nationalism does not make hereditarian claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist-organic representation belongs to the Ustase's fascist strand, not the mainstream.

total-state.rationale: The Ustase aimed at a total state, but the mainstream tradition accepts a constitutional democracy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Tuđman's nationalism spoke of Croatia's historic revival after the Yugoslav period, calling Yugoslavia a mere episode.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Starčević's and Tuđman's Greater Croatia ideas reach for Bosnia, but modern adherents mostly accept present borders; extreme strand excluded.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths of loyalty are alien to a modern republican national movement.

bound-labor.rationale: Starčević opposed feudal privilege in the 19th century; the modern movement never discusses serfdom, so this rests on that older stance.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Croatia is friendly to Israel and diplomatic ties were built under Tuđman; not an ideological tenet.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The HDZ drew heavily on the emigrant community and gave Croats abroad, especially in Bosnia, citizenship and a voice.

revive-national-language.rationale: Croatian is spoken everywhere, so the question of reviving a lost language does not arise; neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: The constitution makes market freedom the basis of the economy and nationalists tied freedom from communism to economic freedom.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement's central claim is the Croatian nation's right to its own sovereign state, set out in the constitution's preamble.

force-without-un.rationale: Croatia sought Western intervention, and Tuđman acted outside international wishes in Bosnia; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christian-democratic adherents do not give reason sole authority over faith.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as a unit that overrides class division, and Radić's party united peasants nationally.

dominated-front.rationale: The movement does not frame itself as a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Radić's national peasant movement organised the lower classes nationally rather than internationally.

ban-interest.rationale: Modern Croatia has a market economy with credit, and nationalists never sought to ban interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The mainstream treats minorities as equal citizens in the constitution; only the Ustase held racial laws.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis; nationalism treats the state as the nation's instrument.

proportional-representation.rationale: Croatia uses proportional lists in electoral districts, with reserved seats for minorities.

national-mission.rationale: Tuđman cast Croatia as part of the West but did not claim a mission to export a system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: HDZ itself was found guilty of corruption, while nationalists have also attacked communist-era elites; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic measures belong to the Ustase's racial ideology, which mainstream modern adherents reject.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Tuđman's side protected veterans and the Homeland War record from prosecution and treats accusations as attacks on the nation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The constitution describes a social state, and HDZ governments run a large public sector.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Starčević saw Croats as a broad nation, and mainstream nationalism does not hold race-mixing doctrines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution guarantees equality before the law, but the movement's history includes exclusion of Serbs and others.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not a Croatian question; nationalists stress the nation's long continuity on its land.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The constitution has one legal order for all citizens, with equal rights to minorities.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Constitution guarantees freedom of religion, though nationalists tie the nation to Catholicism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Meat is normal in Croatia; no support for a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholic religious instruction is in Croatian state schools by concordat, and HDZ defends it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The constitution grounds power in the people and the Croatian nation's sovereign right; the movement asserts popular sovereignty.

population-transfer.rationale: Tuđman's war saw flight and expulsion of Serbs, and critics call that a policy, but adherents officially deny a state policy of expulsion; mainstream rejects it as principle.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not a position the movement takes.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist elements belong to the Ustase's fringe; the mainstream is split or silent.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Croatia's constitution bars anti-constitutional association; adherents are split, as nationalists also fear bans on their own symbols.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Croatian nationalism frames independence as freedom from Habsburg, Hungarian and Serbian domination, though not in republican terms.

separated-powers.rationale: The constitution adopts separation of powers, although Tuđman concentrated power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist idea rejected by nationalists.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Christian-democratic charity versus nationalist focus on the nation; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Croatia sold off state-owned flats to tenants in the early 1990s under Tuđman.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Nationalists worry about low births, not overpopulation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The nationalist case is that Croatia should be a nation-state of Croats, and the conflict with Serbs informs this.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The constitution has election of officials; no support for lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Tuđman's war-time government used emergency powers, but the constitution limits them; split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Tuđman controlled state media but the principle of free media was the formal line.

party-commands-army.rationale: The president, not the party, commands the army under the constitution, though HDZ heavily shaped the army in the 1990s.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: HDZ led Croatia into the EU, and Plenković's HDZ is pro-European, though Tuđman and later nationalists were wary of losing sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The president commands the armed forces under the constitution, which Tuđman's presidency built on.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Catholic Church, governed by bishops, is the national church in the identity of most adherents.

clerical-rule.rationale: Starčević supported separation of church and state and criticised clerical political roles; no clerical rule doctrine.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National defence in the Homeland War is a foundational duty; this defeatist line is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Conservatives sometimes press for it, but the constitution guarantees expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Tuđman won re-election in 1997, but the constitution caps the presidency at two terms.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Croatia joined NATO in 2009 under HDZ, and adherents favour that alliance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The constitution protects property, and nothing supports such a ban.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Homeland War used volunteers in arms but the state built a regular army; mostly rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Radić's peasantist nationalism and the ethos of patriarchal, peasant values mark the tradition.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Tuđman-era nationalists attacked liberal intellectuals as unpatriotic, but the sources show no general claim about the university-educated, so adherents split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalism asserts the Croats' distinct civilisation, placing it in the West rather than the Balkans.

death-penalty.rationale: The constitution abolishes capital punishment, and HDZ governments keep it; some adherents favour it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not a mainstream HDZ line, and Croatia teaches evolution; nationalism has no stance.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Croatian law gives citizenship by descent, including to ethnic Croats abroad, a practice driven by Tuđman's HDZ.

minority-language-support.rationale: The constitution guarantees minority languages, yet nationalist adherents often resist their extension, as with Cyrillic in Vukovar.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The constitution grants religious freedom, but no documented stance on exemptions.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Tuđman's independence project also privatised the economy, but the order was about political sovereignty first.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1990 constitution was passed by the elected parliament, not a separate assembly.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Croatia is a small NATO member with no nuclear ambitions.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The president is directly elected under the constitution, a feature Tuđman exploited.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The Croatian position in the 1990s refused territorial concession, and the Croatian state rests on the claimed historic territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 48 says ownership carries obligations toward the general welfare.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate among Marxists; nationalism rejects the Soviet model without taking sides.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is absent from the nationalist sources; Croatia applies EU rules but the movement itself holds no stance.

collective-defense.rationale: Croatia joined NATO in 2009 under HDZ and the movement treats collective defence as a security guarantee.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Croatia held that Serb-held areas were occupied, a principle adherents apply to their own case.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: HDZ is close to the Catholic Church, though the constitution separates church and state.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Tuđman remained HDZ's leader while president; the constitution requires him to leave party office, but the claim of symbol of unity applied to him anyway.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Croatia's own secession was resisted by force and Croats regard that as aggression; adherents reject the principle.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution binds the president, and the movement's claim is the nation's right, not the ruler's.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Croatian constitution mixes parliament and a directly elected president, but the sources describe no doctrine of mixing few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Tuđmanism cultivated the cult of the first president, with streets, squares and statues named for him.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law questions about shared custody are not covered by the sources; conservative adherents stress the family unit but have no documented line.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist thesis not relevant to nationalism, which rejects socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Starčević's anti-feudalism favoured peasants, but modern HDZ is property-focused and denationalised land.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement demanded return of Croat refugees from Bosnia and Croatia's occupied areas, but resisted Serb return in practice; partly applied.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Tuđman's Bosnia policy and Herzeg-Bosnia advanced such claims, while the modern state disclaims them; the extreme strand holds it, mainstream split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1990 constitution guarantees freedom of religion; that is the state's law rather than a stated nationalist position, though nothing in the movement favours penalties.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a Croatian Catholic principle and contrary to constitutional freedoms.

common-currency.rationale: Croatia adopted the euro in 2023 under a government led by HDZ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The constitution bans association leading to a new South Slav union, and nationalists reject Yugoslavism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The constitution grants minority cultural autonomy, while nationalists have also insisted on the primacy of Croats; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Croatian nationalism pursued a state of its own rather than rights inside others, but Croats in Bosnia also sought rights within that state; adherents split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis that nationalism rejects.

no-bailouts.rationale: Croatia's governments have rescued state-linked firms such as shipyards, and the sources show no doctrine against bailouts; adherents split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Tuđman resisted courts but the constitution has judicial review; split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Ustase insurgency used violence, but mainstream nationalism rejects such tactics.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The constitution establishes equality and a republic.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalists want school history centred on the Croatian nation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Croats were themselves ruled by Austria and Hungary and reject tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Tuđman-era state promoted national pride and symbols in schools.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Mainstream HDZ stands in favour of capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Tuđman sought influence among Bosnian Croats, yet no general doctrine.

delink-world-market.rationale: Croatia sought integration into the EU and world markets.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution has constitutional court protections of rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: The president is elected and Starčević's tradition was popular sovereignty.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority rule with minority rights is the model.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Starčević's resistance to Habsburg and Hungarian rule rested on the claim that they broke Croatian state right.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Party of Rights tradition fought for Sabor's authority against the Habsburg crown and Hungary.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: National activism is a duty in this tradition.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: This is a critical-theory claim; the sources show no nationalist view of mass culture.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the movement.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist parties' independent roads are not a nationalist question; Tito's Yugoslavia took its own road, but nationalists rejected it, so no position.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Tuđman's Bosnia irredentism and the 1990s reclamation of occupied Croatian regions shaped the claim, though mainstream modern adherents accept borders.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The preamble cites the 1943 Antifascist Council, but HDZ and nationalists have often resisted treating Partisan antifascism as the founding value over the independence of 1990-91.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Tuđman's reconciliation policy and HDZ memory politics condemn both communist and Ustase regimes, with an emphasis on communist crimes.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Nationalists defend Homeland War memorials and resist removal, including contested Ustase-linked ones.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Tuđman insisted Croatia belongs in the West, rejecting a separate path.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The constitution places the army under civilian control.

filial-duty.rationale: The conservative family model includes duties to parents.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalists object to foreign control of national assets, but EU rules limit action.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Croatia has mandatory private second-pillar pensions, reformed by HDZ.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The constitution guarantees ownership, and the nationalist tradition honours peasant land title.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Sabor's budget power was part of the state-right claim against Habsburg and Hungarian rule.

single-official-language.rationale: The Croatian Spring fought for the recognition of Croatian as a distinct language, which is the official language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Croatia restricted foreign ownership before EU entry and then opened; split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The legal doctrine is an American framing absent from the sources; no nationalist position is documented.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The sources show no critique of consumerism from the movement, so this is neutral.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Croatia itself was supplied in the 1990s against an arms embargo, but the sources show no doctrine about arming insurgents elsewhere.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: HDZ pursues family and birth policy because of demographic decline.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not covered by the sources; Croatian coastal debates exist but the movement has no stated stance.

job-guarantee.rationale: Communist-era job guarantee is what nationalists left.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Conservative adherents hold a duty to obey law.

non-intervention.rationale: Croatia asked for foreign help, but Tuđman also rejected foreign interference in Bosnia.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Ustase held antisemitic and anti-Serb conspiracy claims, but mainstream modern adherents reject them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is protected in the 2013 constitutional definition.

local-production.rationale: Peasantist tradition, but no modern doctrine.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement organises through a party.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The sovereignty clause is inalienable, but Croatia has accepted EU and ICTY law, so this is only partly held.

religious-nation.rationale: Starčević counted Catholics, Muslims and Orthodox as Croats, but Catholicism is tied to identity in HDZ; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Croatian nationalism arose in revolt against domination by Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The state is unitary, though regions like Istria press for this.

defeat-communism.rationale: The movement defined itself against communist Yugoslavia and the Tuđman era is anti-communist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not covered by the sources; HDZ governments use both public and private providers, so adherents split.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement ties the nation to the Catholic Church, so the Marxist view of religion is rejected; the sources do not argue the point directly.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Croatian language movement has sought native words over Serbian and international forms since the Croatian Spring and in the 1990s.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not nationalist; Yugoslavia had cooperatives and the movement abandoned them.

majority-settlement.rationale: Post-war Croatia encouraged Croat settlement in the former occupied areas, a practice critics call a policy; adherents deny it is principle.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Ustase claimed a third way, but mainstream HDZ embraced capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The constitution's preamble grounds the state in the historic state right of the Croatian nation; it does not compare that claim against the claims of other peoples now living in Croatia.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The mainstream condemns the Ustase's crimes officially, though Tuđman was criticised for downplaying numbers; denial is fringe.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Croatia decriminalised in 1977 and HDZ governments did not recriminalise; even social conservatives accept that.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Tuđman's authoritarian practice repressed critics, but formal doctrine is multiparty.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine foreign to Croatian nationalism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An Islamist doctrine alien to the movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Starčević counted Muslims as Croats and Bosnian Muslims have a role in Croatian history, though some adherents are hostile; split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The constitution calls Croatia a social state with market freedom, and HDZ sits in the Christian-democratic family.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Croatia joined NATO and the EU under HDZ.

property-franchise.rationale: The constitution grants universal suffrage, as Starčević favoured.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A leftist critique of media ownership; HDZ-era governments themselves controlled media, so the sources do not show nationalists endorsing it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The constitution provides for law and public promulgation.

racial-franchise.rationale: Starčević used a broad Croat identity, not a racial franchise; the constitution has universal suffrage.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not covered by the sources; Croatia has a freedom-of-information law, but the movement has no distinct line.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Ustase boycotted Serb and Jewish businesses, but mainstream modern adherents reject that.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are absent from the sources; the movement relies on parties and elections, so this is a neutral inference.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The sources show HDZ-linked privatisation concentrated wealth, but no nationalist doctrine on wealth and liberty is documented.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Tuđman partitioned Bosnia but Croatia's constitution reserves minority seats; split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Christian-democratic adherents value church charity, but the sources record no stance, and HDZ governments run a large welfare state.

term-limits.rationale: The constitution has presidential term limits only.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is absent from the nationalist sources; the movement's demographic worries concern national decline instead.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Catholic Church excludes women from priesthood.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Modern Croatian law has equal spouses; conservative adherents accept it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: EU citizens vote locally; not a nationalist principle.

rent-control.rationale: Housing rent caps are not covered by the sources; Croatia has had protected-tenancy rules from socialist times, and adherents split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Tuđman's policy sought unity of Croats across the Croatia-Bosnia border, and he spoke of Croatia as an apple with a bite taken out of it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Article 48 guarantees ownership, which covers personal belongings as well as productive property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Homeland War is the founding act of the modern state and is framed as lawful defence, and the Catholic-leaning tradition accepts just self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The constitution's preamble grounds the Croatian state in an unbroken thousand-year historic state right, and Starcevic's state-right doctrine rests on it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Homeland War dead, especially at Vukovar, are honoured in near-sacred national commemoration, which Tudjmanism cultivated.

culture-before-state.rationale: Starcevic's Party of Rights and later Tudjman put the sovereign state and its historic right first, with culture following from it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution protects market freedom and HDZ privatised heavily, yet public services stayed largely public; split.

second-chamber.rationale: Croatia had a second chamber, the Chamber of Counties, from 1993 to 2001, and an upper chamber suits the state-right tradition, though it was later abolished.

municipal-property.rationale: HDZ privatised enterprises into private hands; the constitution guarantees property and market freedom.

person-over-state.rationale: The constitution protects individual rights, but Tuđmanism put the nation's state-building above individual claims; split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: HDZ is Christian-democratic and Catholic-leaning, and the constitution invokes the nation's tradition, though Starčević was secular.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The mainstream defines Croats as a nation by state right and territory, not race, and excludes Ustase racial politics.

racial-pride.rationale: Mainstream Croatian nationalism rests on national, not racial, pride; racial pride belongs to the disowned Ustase extreme.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Homeland War was a defensive war of independence, but Tuđmanism also pursued aims in Bosnia; split.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition policy is not part of the nationalist doctrine and HDZ-led governments have mixed free and paid study; adherents split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The tradition has no doctrine on women's distinct public values, and conservative and modern adherents differ.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Homeland War is treated as a sacred founding, so refusing to fight a war between states cuts against the mainstream.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Croatia is a small open economy and the tradition did not address world economic rules; adherents are split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Mainstream Croatian nationalism built and defends the state set out in the 1990 constitution and rejects revolutionary overthrow.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The constitution protects natural resources as state-protected goods, but the tradition did not address pricing nature; adherents are split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Tudjman's nationalism treated the nation and its independence struggle as a sacred community, and the constitution grounds it in centuries of state right.

public-service-media.rationale: The constitution guarantees media freedom but Tudjmanism controlled public media; the tradition is split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Croatian nationalism holds Croatian to be a distinct national language, separate from Serbian, and rejects the one-language view.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The constitution separates religious communities from the state and makes them equal before the law, though the Catholic Church has a privileged agreement in practice.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Mainstream nationalists accept competitive elections but tie legitimacy to national sovereignty and state right; the sources do not settle it.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1990 constitution guarantees equality of the sexes and Croatian nationalism has not contested women's vote or office.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The HDZ cooperated with the Hague tribunal under pressure but Tudmanism resisted its judgments on the Homeland War, so adherents are split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Croatian nationalism in its mainstream form is anti-communist and rejected the Yugoslav socialist state, so defending such a state is opposed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Croatia held a plebiscite for its own independence in 1991 but refused one for Serb-held areas, so the principle is applied selectively.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The constitution's preamble grounds the nation in its historic homeland, and the movement's state-right doctrine treats the land as national inheritance.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Croatian nationalism treats Croats in Bosnia and elsewhere abroad as part of the nation and the HDZ has supported them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Adherents split in principle: HDZ privatisation favoured connected firms, but the mainstream formally endorses a market economy.

automate-paid-work.rationale: No documented position; conservative stress on work and jobs competes with modernisation, so adherents are split.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Starcevic and Radic's peasant movement linked nation and common people, but HDZ's practice favours business too, so adherents are split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The tradition is anti-communist and the constitution guarantees market freedom and plural democracy, which contradict one-party socialist rule.

missingStatements.text: A nation's right to a state of its own rests on its historic statehood, not only on the will of its present population.
missingStatements.rationale: The constitution's preamble grounds Croatia in an unbroken state right going back to the Middle Ages, and Starčević built his party on it.

missingStatements.text: A country's wartime past should be commemorated in a way that honours its own national struggle for independence over internationally agreed narratives.
missingStatements.rationale: Tuđmanism fought over the memory of Jasenovac and the Ustase, and treated its Homeland War as a sacred founding.
missingStatements.declined: Commemoration of national wars is specific to one country and not a general question across ideologies.

missingStatements.text: A country should not join any association of states that could recreate a former union it left.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 141 of the constitution forbids association leading to a renewed South Slav or Balkan state community.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Croatian constitution; pool-sovereignty covers the general question.

notes: Adherents split on Ustase-era memory, treatment of Serbs, Bosnian Croat claims and Church-state ties. The Ustase strand would answer the exclusion and racial statements very differently. Many economic and social answers are inferred from HDZ practice, which is why confidences are mostly low.
